history.dynasty: Holkar (rebuilt 1787 by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore)
history.period: Rebuilt 1787 CE; earlier shrine of unknown date
history.summary: Vishnupad Temple is a Hindu Vaishnavite temple on the banks of the Phalgu river in Gaya, Bihar, dedicated to Vishnu. Its sanctum holds the Dharmasila, a basalt block incised with a 40-cm footprint said to be Vishnu's, left when he subdued the demon Gayasura. The present octagonal, east-facing granite temple with a ~30-metre shikhara was rebuilt in 1787 by Ahilyabai Holkar using Munger black stone and craftsmen brought from Rajasthan. It is the centre of Shraddha/pind daan rites in Gaya, with the Gayawal Brahmins as traditional priests. name: Vishnupad Temple
town_description: Gaya is an ancient city in south Bihar on the banks of the Phalgu river, one of Hinduism's most important pilgrimage centres for ancestral rites (pind daan). It sits adjacent to Bodh Gaya, Buddhism's holiest site, making the city a joint hub of Hindu and Buddhist pilgrimage. Gaya is well connected by rail and has its own international airport.

travel.road: In Gaya town, easily reached by road from Bodh Gaya (~12-16 km) and Patna (~110 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Pitru Paksha (September-October) is the peak pilgrimage season for pind daan
